cards.headline: Single-car crash on Donald Ross Road in Jupiter kills one Sunday morning
cards.teaser: A single-vehicle crash on Donald Ross Road in Jupiter Sunday morning killed one person, according to Jupiter police officials.
cards.body:
A single-vehicle crash on Donald Ross Road in Jupiter Sunday morning killed one person, according to Jupiter police officials. The crash happened just before 6 a.m. when the driver came over railroad tracks, lost control of the vehicle, and struck a tree. Police confirmed one adult male died in the crash but are withholding the victim's name pending notification of next of kin.

Both eastbound and westbound lanes of Donald Ross Road between Military Trail and Alternate A1A were closed for several hours as crash investigators worked the scene. The roadway has since reopened to traffic. The Jupiter Police Department is continuing to investigate the circumstances that led to the fatal crash.

cards.headline: Indiantown brush fire grows to 125 acres, now 99% contained after weekend escalation
cards.teaser: A brush fire that began Friday in Indiantown escalated over the weekend before being brought under near-total control, according to Martin County Fire Rescue an.
cards.body:
A brush fire that began Friday in Indiantown escalated over the weekend before being brought under near-total control, according to Martin County Fire Rescue and the Florida Forest Service. The fire now covers approximately 125 acres and is 99% contained as of Sunday morning.

Martin County Fire Rescue firefighters first responded to the rapidly developing brush fire in the 2600 block of Southwest Warfield Boulevard just before 3:30 p.m. on Friday, June 5. Crews quickly contained the blaze at approximately 37.8 acres, with no reported injuries and no structures threatened at the time. The Florida Forest Service assisted by establishing plow lines to stop the spread of flames, while MCFR's drone team identified remaining hotspots before crews cleared the area. Officials said the fire's cause was unknown, though early indications suggested it may have been a holdover fire, meaning a lightning strike could have smoldered underground for days before igniting visible flames.

By Saturday, June 6, the situation escalated significantly when crews returned to the same area to battle a much larger 120-acre brush fire. Officials believe the fire rekindled from the previous day's incident. Shifting winds and dense vegetation contributed to rapid fire growth, prompting a large-scale response from Martin County Fire Rescue, the Florida Forest Service, and the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Firefighters worked to protect nearby structures as smoke spread across the area, though officials confirmed there was no broader threat to the public. Residents were advised to expect smoky conditions throughout the weekend as suppression efforts continued.

The Florida Forest Service remains in the area monitoring conditions to ensure no further flare-ups occur. Authorities say the investigation into the fire's origin remains ongoing.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Commissioner Weiss responds to teen takeover threat at Wellington Green Mall
cards.teaser: A social media post promoting a teen takeover at the Wellington Green Mall gained nearly 100,000 views, prompting the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office to increase law enforcement presence and Commissioner Greg Weiss to call for parental involvement.
cards.body:
A social media post promoting a teen takeover at Wellington Green Mall gained nearly 100,000 views, prompting the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office to increase law enforcement presence at the mall. Teen takeovers are large gatherings of teens at malls, beaches or parks that typically devolve into violence. The trend has been spreading across Florida, including an event in Clearwater at the end of May that resulted in widespread property damage, fights and the shooting of a 17-year-old. Shoppers at Wellington Green Mall on Friday noticed the heightened police presence. Savanna Restrepo, who was picking up her son Isaac from summer camp, said the visible police presence was reassuring. Fellow parent Eric Delgado said the response was the right call. Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier called the events "unacceptable" and announced a plan to investigate and prosecute those responsible.

Palm Beach County Commissioner Greg Weiss said community safety is a priority but pointed to a root cause. With school out and teens having more time on their hands, Weiss said parents should take steps to fill that time through community rec centers and programming offered by cities and county facilities. Weiss acknowledged that summer camp costs can be a barrier for some families and noted that Palm Beach County offers scholarship opportunities for summer camps. He emphasized that the bottom line is parental involvement, urging parents to know what their kids are doing and stay in contact with them.

cards.headline: Lt. Gov. Jay Collins to Unveil Senior Protection Initiative Monday as Governor Campaign Intensifies
cards.body:
Lt. Gov. Jay Collins will host a news conference Monday at 10 a.m. at McCall's Tavern on Alverez Ave. to present details about his "Live Florida" initiative. The comprehensive plan focuses on helping Florida seniors remain financially secure and independent during their retirement years. Collins is using the announcement as part of his campaign for Governor.

The initiative addresses major financial challenges confronting Florida's growing senior population, including rising housing costs, insurance premiums, healthcare expenses, and everyday living costs. Collins will outline proposals to reduce elderly fraud and cybersecurity threats that target retirees while also presenting increased consumer protections and public safety measures designed to improve seniors' quality of life. He previously established Operation Senior Shield in November while serving as Lieutenant Governor, a program that sends timely text and email alerts to help older adults and their caregivers stay informed about scammer tactics. During a Jacksonville launch event last year, Collins explained the program's purpose. "Senior Shield provides timely text and email alerts, so older adults and caregivers can stay ahead of scammers," he said. "We're going to make you hard targets. You have to have the information to understand what's going on. When a new threat appears, Floridians will know about it before the scammers get to their door, their inbox, or their phone."

Collins faces significant competition in the Republican Primary Election scheduled for August 18. He is running against U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, who currently leads in the party contest. Collins acknowledged the challenging circumstances but expressed frustration with his opponent's reluctance to engage in debates. During an appearance on Fox News' "Sunday Morning Futures," Collins criticized Donalds directly. "You can't hide in the shadows. You can't pull a Biden and hide in a corner behind your couch in the basement. You've got to come out and debate, and I'm very frustrated that Byron Donalds is unwilling to do that. I think he's got to stand up and show up. If you're that far ahead, then what are you scared of? Step up, communicate, show up at a debate stage," Collins said.

Collins serves as the Republican lieutenant to Gov. Ron DeSantis and has positioned senior protections as a key element of his gubernatorial platform. The winner of the August primary will advance to the General Election. Collins' emphasis on senior financial security reflects his broader campaign message about affordability for Florida's older residents.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie 9-year-old launches junior chess club to share love of the game
cards.teaser: Orion Jean Baptiste, a 9-year-old from Port St. Lucie, has launched a new juniors chess club that now meets every Friday at Port St. Lucie and will soon begin two more programs at the Fenn Center in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
A new juniors chess club has launched in Port St. Lucie, inspired by 9-year-old Orion Jean Baptiste who wanted to share his love of the game with his community. Baptiste's passion for chess began at age 5, playing alongside family members. "I just wanted kids to learn about chess," Baptiste said. He hopes to pass that passion on to others, noting that many people focus on technology instead of board games. "I'm hoping that more people have respect for board games," Baptiste said.

The Atlantis Chess Club now meets every Friday in Port St. Lucie and has already attracted more than 36 junior members of all skill levels. Diana Cowan Kempton, the club's program director, said chess will help develop the next generation by building "leaders or members that are more focused, more patient, more strategic and thoughtful in their decision making." Thomas Furlong, a father who brought his children to the club, said the setting is ideal for his family. The club will soon begin two more programs at the Fenn Center in Fort Pierce.

cards.headline: Pride on the Block fills West Palm Beach with celebration and support for LGBTQ+ community
cards.teaser: A vibrant celebration filled The Peach in West Palm Beach Saturday as Pride on the Block brought together neighbors, allies, and activists, serving as the largest fundraiser for Transpire Help.
cards.body:
A vibrant celebration of love and identity filled The Peach in West Palm Beach Saturday as Pride on the Block brought together neighbors, allies, and activists in support of the LGBTQ+ community. The event serves as the largest fundraiser for Transpire Help, a non-profit organization that provides substance use treatment, mental health care, and stable housing to LGBTQ+ individuals. Donna Weinberger, founder of Transpire Help, said the event creates a space where attendees can feel celebrated and safe. "People can come and be filled with unity and joy and happiness and be able to be in one spot and feel safe," Weinberger said.

For performers like Liam Chambers, the event carries deep personal meaning. Chambers credits Transpire Help with helping turn his life around, noting he is three years sober and now performs as a drag king. Transpire Help's services are especially critical as cuts to government funding have slashed the number of people the organization can help in half. According to Weinberger, a significant portion of the community, particularly gender diverse individuals, lack health insurance or funds to access treatment, making the fundraiser more important than ever.

cards.headline: 35 foster youth graduate at ChildNet celebration at Palm Beach State College
cards.teaser: 35 students walked across the stage at ChildNet's annual graduation celebration at Palm Beach State College, marking a milestone for foster youth and young adults served by the Broward and Palm Beach County nonprofit.
cards.body:
35 students walked across the stage at ChildNet's annual graduation celebration at Palm Beach State College, marking a milestone for foster youth and young adults served by the Broward and Palm Beach County nonprofit. ChildNet supports foster kids and young men and women through education, adoptions and independent living resources.

Among the graduates were Sabrina Diaz and Brian Saintfort, both of whom lost a parent and turned to ChildNet for support. The organization equipped them with the resources they needed to move forward. Diaz shared a message for others in similar situations, urging them to believe they will be big one day and to never give up on school and dreams. Saintfort echoed that message. Larry N. Rein, CEO of ChildNet, reflected on the significance of the evening, calling it the fruition of great work by everyone in the community, including case workers at ChildNet and DCF, and especially the kids who have worked so hard. Diaz is already enrolled in pre-med classes at Palm Beach State College, where she hopes to become a doctor. Saintfort plans to pursue a vocational program to become a plumber.

cards.headline: Jupiter Island faces critical erosion threatening to split island at Peck Lake
cards.teaser: Nearly the entire coastline of Jupiter Island is critically eroded, with a new state report warning the ocean could break through at Peck Lake and potentially split the island in half.
cards.body:
A 2025 Florida Department of Environmental Protection report warns that Jupiter Island's 11.5-mile shoreline has eroded so severely that the ocean could break through at Peck Lake, potentially splitting the island in half. The threat stretches from Blowing Rocks Preserve, where private development is already at risk, to Peck Lake, where a breach could turn a thin strip of land into an open inlet. A storm previously breached Peck Lake in the early 1960s before the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers filled it back in with sand. Mark Perry with the Florida Oceanographic Society said a future breach could upend ecosystems that depend on a delicate balance of fresh and saltwater to survive.

The report identifies multiple sites at risk, including the Joseph Reed Mound, a 3,000- to 4,000-year-old archaeological site already half lost to erosion, along with Blowing Rocks Preserve, Hobe Sound Wildlife Refuge, and St. Lucie Inlet Preserve State Park. Perry noted there are over 33 threatened and endangered species in those areas. Jupiter Island Commissioner Marshall Field said the town completed a major beach renourishment project in April 2025, dumping enough sand to fill nearly 400 Olympic-sized swimming pools. About $3 million in town taxpayer dollars goes toward beach renourishment annually. Field said the town will continue this work as long as funding remains available.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County rental assistance program overwhelmed as demand far exceeds funding
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County receives nearly 8,000 calls for housing assistance per month, but emergency rental assistance funding can only help a fraction of those in need.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County's Community Services Department has nearly $2 million in combined grant funding for its Emergency Rental Assistance Program, designed to help residents who can't pay rent. However, demand far exceeds available resources each month. "We're doing what we can to prioritize and serve those who are most needy but the demand far outweighs the resources that are available," said program director Dr. James Green. Applications open at the beginning of each month but fill quickly. According to Green, there are nearly 8,000 calls for housing assistance per month based on data combined with 211. The county currently has about 800 applications in the queue for rental assistance, typically receiving about 600 applications within the first couple of hours they're open. At the time of reporting, the county's assistance portal was marked closed due to high demand.

Rental prices have pushed many residents to financial crisis. According to the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the average rent for a one-bedroom in Palm Beach County is $2,020 a month. Green attributed the recent surge in applications partly to rising costs of living, including housing, gas, and food. For residents unable to access the county's program, 211 offers another option, connecting people with nonprofits and other assistance programs in the area. Green urges anyone in need to call 1-833-CSD-WILL to check for availability.

cards.headline: Okeechobee County woman sues Campbell Soup, Walmart over worms in SpaghettiOs
cards.teaser: Mary Hubbard claims she and her daughter developed parasitic infections after finding live worms in SpaghettiOs purchased at the Walmart Supercenter on South Parrott Avenue in Okeechobee.
cards.body:
A woman from Okeechobee County is suing Campbell Soup Co. and Walmart after claiming she and her daughter found live worms in their SpaghettiOs. Mary Hubbard says she and her daughter developed parasitic infections and other medical complications following the incident. According to the complaint, Hubbard purchased the SpaghettiOs in June 2024 at the Walmart Supercenter store on South Parrott Avenue in Okeechobee.

Hubbard's attorneys state she discovered what appeared to be worms or parasites actively moving within the food. The complaint notes that Hubbard documented the contamination in multiple videos, which clearly depict worm-like organisms moving within the food product. The lawsuit alleges the companies failed to properly inspect the product and seeks $50,000 in damages. Campbell said the claims lack merit, while Walmart said it is reviewing the court filing.

cards.headline: Florida voters divided on property tax proposal ahead of November ballot
cards.teaser: Florida voters will decide this November whether to roll back property taxes by raising the homestead exemption, a measure drawing mixed reactions from residents.
cards.body:
Florida voters will decide this November whether to roll back property taxes by raising the homestead exemption for homeowners, a proposal drawing mixed reactions from West Palm Beach residents. The ballot measure requires 60% approval to pass, following a similar proposal that failed in 2018.

Homeowners expressed general support for the tax reduction. Brian Edington said he supports the idea because it benefits people who permanently live in Florida, noting he is comfortable with local governments spending less. He pointed to his own neighborhood as an example where cuts could be made, saying trash services pick up twice weekly but once weekly would be adequate. However, renters expressed more skepticism about the proposal's benefits. One renter spoken with along Clematis Avenue in downtown West Palm Beach on Friday said the savings would not reach renters, predicting landlords would raise rent on everybody. Rosabella Olivares, a shopper in West Palm Beach, expressed concern about reduced funding, saying there's going to be less money because everything is expensive now.

cards.headline: Florida could ban Fourth of July fireworks due to severe drought conditions
cards.teaser: State leaders are weighing whether to ban fireworks for the 250th anniversary of American independence as drought conditions across Florida worsen.
cards.body:
Florida's Fourth of July celebrations could look significantly different this year as state leaders monitor severe drought conditions and consider whether to ban fireworks for the nation's 250th anniversary. The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services reports that this year's drought is more severe than 1998, the last time a statewide fireworks ban was implemented. The entire state is at least abnormally dry, with Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast experiencing moderate to extreme drought conditions.

Florida Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson warned in May that a ban is possible if drought conditions persist through July Fourth. "If we're still in drought conditions come Fourth of July, absolutely. We're talking about obviously, potentially hundreds of thousands of people going out doing fireworks. You could put the entire state on fire in evening all over the state all at one time," Simpson said. He acknowledged the significance of the 250th celebration but urged residents to consider alternatives. At Sky King Fireworks in West Palm Beach, owner Bill Murphy said the store has seen increased customer activity ahead of the holiday. Murphy monitors drought conditions closely but remains cautiously optimistic, noting there is plenty of rain in the forecast. The Department of Agriculture said a fireworks ban would be a last resort.

cards.headline: Indian River, Martin and St. Lucie counties enforce summer fertilizer ban starting June 30
cards.teaser: Residents in Indian River, Martin and St. Lucie counties will be prohibited from using any fertilizer containing phosphorus or nitrogen starting June 30.
cards.body:
Starting June 30, Indian River, Martin and St. Lucie counties will enforce a ban on any fertilizer containing phosphorus or nitrogen. The restriction applies to both residential lawns and landscaping projects. According to Jordan Skaggs with Environmental Resources in St. Lucie County, the ban targets nutrient-rich runoff during the rainy season that can cause algae blooms in waterways like the Indian River Lagoon and St. Lucie River.

Harmful algae blooms create significant environmental problems. Skaggs explained that the blooms can shade out beneficial plants that fish and wildlife depend on. At certain densities, these blooms can release toxins that affect human health, wildlife health and overall ecosystem health. Grantly Ricketts, director of University of Florida's Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences St. Lucie County Extension, recommends composting as an alternative during the ban. Ricketts described composting as being like a small trash can, calling it "the easiest and most practical way or means to add nutrients to your landscape."

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie 9-year-old launches junior chess club to teach board game strategy
hero.body:
Orion Jean Baptiste, a 9-year-old Port St. Lucie resident, has created a new junior chess club designed to introduce young people to the strategic board game. Baptiste developed his own passion for chess starting at age 5 while playing with family members, and he now wants to share that enthusiasm with others in his community. The Atlantis Chess Club meets every Friday at the Port St. Lucie library and has already enrolled more than 36 junior members.

Baptiste's motivation for starting the club stems from a desire to shift young people's attention away from technology. "Everybody's more focused on like tech stuff," Baptiste said. "I'm hoping that more people have respect for board games." Diana Cowan Kempton, the club's program director, believes chess offers valuable developmental benefits for the next generation. She explained that the game can help build young leaders who are more focused, patient, strategic, and thoughtful when making decisions. The club welcomes players at all skill levels, making it accessible to beginners and experienced players alike.

Families have embraced the club as a place where children can learn together and develop healthy competition. Thomas Furlong brought both his daughter and son to the club, recognizing it as an opportunity for his daughter to learn chess while giving his son a chance to improve his skills. The sibling dynamic creates friendly competition that benefits both children. For Francesca Furlong, a newer member of the club, the most appealing aspect is straightforward: playing with other kids her age provides enjoyment and social connection alongside skill development.

The club's success at the Port St. Lucie library location has led to expansion plans. The Atlantis Chess Club will soon launch two additional programs at the Fenn Center in Fort Pierce, allowing more young people across the region to participate. Baptiste's simple goal of helping kids learn chess has resonated with families seeking enriching activities that encourage strategic thinking and patience. As the club continues to grow, it demonstrates how one young person's passion for a traditional board game can inspire community engagement and provide meaningful learning opportunities for dozens of other children.

hero.headline: Broadway's 'Beetlejuice' Musical Runs Through June 7 at Kravis Center in West Palm Beach
hero.teaser: The Broadway hit brings its spooky humor and over-the-top visuals to the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall with performances through Saturday.
hero.body:
Broadway hit Beetlejuice the musical is playing at the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach through June 7, bringing spooky humor, over-the-top visuals, and heartwarming moments to Palm Beach County. Actor Ryan Stajmiger steps into the iconic striped suit to play the mischievous demon beloved from Tim Burton's 1988 film. The musical follows Lydia Deetz, a strange and unusual teen, whose life changes after meeting two recently deceased neighbors and a demon with a flair for trouble.

Stajmiger says one of his favorite parts is laughing with the audience. He gets to break the fourth wall and communicate directly with audience members. Very early in the run, he experienced an unexpected moment when a wig change went wrong. Stajmiger wears two wigs, and the second wig came off with the first wig, leaving him bald for an entire scene.

Performances include 7:30 p.m. shows on June 3 and June 4, 8 p.m. on June 5, matinee and evening performances on June 6, and a closing matinee on June 7. Tickets start at $34.50 and are available at kravis.org. The show is recommended for ages 13 and up, with parental discretion advised.

cards.headline: 80-Mile Ocean Paddle from Bahamas to Lake Worth Beach Set for June 13 to Raise Cystic Fibrosis Funds
cards.body:
More than 100 paddlers will cross 80 miles of the open Atlantic Ocean this June as part of the annual Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis. Event founder Travis Suit said participants will launch from Bimini, Bahamas, at midnight on June 13 and arrive at Lake Worth Beach after 12 to 16 hours of paddling. The endurance trek benefits the Piper's Angels Foundation, which Suit established to honor his daughter, Piper, who was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at age 4.

The four-day event begins June 10 with arrivals and a poolside social at Bimini Cove. Thursday includes a 4Ocean beach cleanup and community buffet dinner, while Friday features a Paddle Out Rose Ceremony to honor cystic fibrosis warriors, followed by rest and safety checks before launch night. All paddlers must wear U.S. Coast Guard-approved personal flotation devices, waterproof whistles, and reflective gear during dark hours. GPS trackers provided by the event must be worn and active throughout the crossing, and mandatory safety meetings will be held. Paddlers must raise at least $2,000, while crew or virtual participants have a $500 minimum. Final contributions are due July 31. Spectators are invited to Lake Worth Beach on June 13 for a daylong celebration welcoming the paddlers. For registration and donations, visit crossingforcysticfibrosis.com and pipersangels.org.

hero.headline: Lt. Gov. Jay Collins to Unveil Senior Protection Initiative Monday as Governor Campaign Intensifies
hero.body:
Lt. Gov. Jay Collins will host a news conference Monday at 10 a.m. at McCall's Tavern on Alverez Ave. to present details about his "Live Florida" initiative. The comprehensive plan focuses on helping Florida seniors remain financially secure and independent during their retirement years. Collins is using the announcement as part of his campaign for Governor.

The initiative addresses major financial challenges confronting Florida's growing senior population, including rising housing costs, insurance premiums, healthcare expenses, and everyday living costs. Collins will outline proposals to reduce elderly fraud and cybersecurity threats that target retirees while also presenting increased consumer protections and public safety measures designed to improve seniors' quality of life. He previously established Operation Senior Shield in November while serving as Lieutenant Governor, a program that sends timely text and email alerts to help older adults and their caregivers stay informed about scammer tactics. During a Jacksonville launch event last year, Collins explained the program's purpose. "Senior Shield provides timely text and email alerts, so older adults and caregivers can stay ahead of scammers," he said. "We're going to make you hard targets. You have to have the information to understand what's going on. When a new threat appears, Floridians will know about it before the scammers get to their door, their inbox, or their phone."

Collins faces significant competition in the Republican Primary Election scheduled for August 18. He is running against U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, who currently leads in the party contest. Collins acknowledged the challenging circumstances but expressed frustration with his opponent's reluctance to engage in debates. During an appearance on Fox News' "Sunday Morning Futures," Collins criticized Donalds directly. "You can't hide in the shadows. You can't pull a Biden and hide in a corner behind your couch in the basement. You've got to come out and debate, and I'm very frustrated that Byron Donalds is unwilling to do that. I think he's got to stand up and show up. If you're that far ahead, then what are you scared of? Step up, communicate, show up at a debate stage," Collins said.

Collins serves as the Republican lieutenant to Gov. Ron DeSantis and has positioned senior protections as a key element of his gubernatorial platform. The winner of the August primary will advance to the General Election. Collins' emphasis on senior financial security reflects his broader campaign message about affordability for Florida's older residents.

cards.headline: Germans Emerge as Top Foreign Searchers for South Florida Real Estate as Retirement Planning Trend Grows
cards.teaser: Germany has become the number one foreign country searching for South Florida real estate online, according to the Miami Association of Realtors, reflecting a shift in how Germans view Florida as a long-term retirement plan.
cards.body:
Germany has recently become the top foreign country searching for South Florida real estate online, according to the Miami Association of Realtors. This represents a significant shift in how Germans view Florida, increasingly considering it as a retirement destination rather than merely a vacation spot. Many German buyers are searching for property years in advance of making a permanent move, with some easing into Florida life over years or decades before imagining it as the place where they will spend the rest of their lives.

German buyers are attracted to Florida's sunshine, space, private property, and what they perceive as a manageable level of government interference compared to Germany. Property taxes in Florida appear refreshingly transparent to Germans accustomed to income taxes, social contributions, inheritance concerns, energy levies, real estate transfer taxes, and extensive regulations. Foreigners can purchase homes without major restrictions and experience a straightforward purchasing process that moves quickly, which can feel surprisingly uncomplicated compared to the layers of permits and administrative hurdles typical in Europe. One German homeowner has owned Florida property for 16 years and now spends roughly half the year in the state after obtaining a Green Card. International buyers contribute to local economies by hiring property managers, contractors, landscapers, pool service companies, and real estate agents while adding to the tax base.

cards.headline: Five Florida House Districts Remain Unchallenged Despite Competitive Voter Margins Ahead of Qualifying Deadline
cards.teaser: Less than a week from the qualifying deadline, five competitive Florida House seats remain unchallenged by one of the two major political parties, ranging from districts decided by 1 percentage point to 11 points in the 2024 presidential election.
cards.body:
Less than a week before the qualifying deadline, 25 Florida House district races remain uncontested by one of the two major political parties. While this arrangement is understandable in 80% of those contests where one party holds a significant electoral advantage, five House districts have narrow enough voter divides that the absence of an opposing party challenger is confounding. Two of these districts are Republican-controlled and three are Democrat-led.

The competitive districts range from a Palm Beach County seat that sided with Kamala Harris in 2024 by just 1 percentage point to an Orange County district Harris won by 11 points, roughly matching President Donald Trump's margin in House District 87. Democratic Rep. Emily Gregory flipped that Jupiter district in a March upset. The other three races are set in Duval, Miami-Dade, and Pinellas counties with even smaller divides between Democrats and Republicans. The Florida Democratic Party stated it has invested in year-round organizing and candidate recruitment, with over 1,300 Democrats expressing interest in running over the last 18 months. Republican Party of Florida Chair Evan Power expressed confidence his party will grow its supermajority in the Legislature. The Primary Election is scheduled for Aug. 18, followed by the General Election.

cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis announced the appointment of Alexandria Hill and Kevin Payne to the St. Johns River State College District Board of Trustees. Richard Komando, Willard "Judd" Sapp Jr., and Tammy "Chereese" Stewart were reappointed to the board. The Florida Senate must confirm the appointments. St. Johns River State College operates three campuses in Orange Park, Palatka, and St. Augustine with approximately 8,000 combined student enrollment.

Hill is active in the Clay County community and serves on the Clay County Development Authority. She is a Partner in the Driver, McAfee, Hawthorne and Dibenow law firm. She holds a bachelor's degree in finance and marketing from Stetson University and a law degree from the University of Florida. Payne serves as Senior Manager of Contracting for Imagine 360 health insurance company and President of the Jacksonville Association of Health Underwriters. He earned a bachelor's degree in accounting from the University of Texas and a master's degree in business administration from Oklahoma City University. Komando is a Partner in the Bradley, Garrison and Komando law firm and has served as Circuit Director and Statewide General Counsel for the Fourth Judicial Circuit Guardian ad Litem Office for Northeast Florida. Stewart is the Assistant County Manager for the Clay County Commission and a member of the Clay County Development Authority, Clay County Cattlemen Association, Clay County Farm Bureau, and the Florida Planning and Zoning Association.

cards.headline: Rep. Byron Donalds Defends Trump Administration Iran Actions as National Security Necessity
cards.teaser: Florida Rep. Byron Donalds said President Donald Trump made the right call to stop Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons, arguing that ongoing actions against Iran do not contradict Trump's campaign message about avoiding new wars.
cards.body:
Rep. Byron Donalds defended President Donald Trump's actions against Iran on Newsmax's Sunday Agenda, arguing that ongoing operations do not contradict Trump's campaign promise to avoid starting foreign wars. Donalds said the administration had to address the reality that Iran was enriching nuclear material to weapons-grade levels. He characterized Iran as a theocratic dictatorship that has lied about its ballistic missile capabilities, claiming a 4,000-mile range that is twice what was previously stated and capable of reaching Europe and U.S. bases there. Donalds said Iran cannot be trusted over the last 47 years because it is committed to radical Sharia law, which he said is incompatible with Western civilization.

Trump addressed the Iran situation on NBC's Meet the Press with Kristen Welker on Sunday, saying he did not guarantee no war and does not like endless wars. He characterized the current situation differently, stating operations have continued for three months with much of it under a ceasefire. Trump said the blockade has been effective and the threat is largely over. Donalds said Trump made the right decision to stop Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie 9-year-old Orion Jean Baptiste launches junior chess club
hero.teaser: Orion Jean Baptiste, a 9-year-old from Port St. Lucie, launched a new juniors chess club to share his love of the game with his community.
hero.body:
Orion Jean Baptiste, a 9-year-old from Port St. Lucie, has inspired the creation of a new junior chess club in his community. Baptiste's interest in chess started when he was 5 years old, playing the game with family members. Now he wants to share that passion with other young people in the area. "I just wanted kids to learn about chess," Baptiste explained. He believes that board games deserve more respect, particularly since many people are focused on technology instead.

The club has already attracted a diverse group of players with varying levels of experience. Thomas Furlong, a father who brought his children to participate, said the club offered something valuable for his family. He saw it as an opportunity for his daughter to learn chess fundamentals while his son could continue improving his skills. Their daughter, Francesca, enjoys the social aspect of the club. "Playing with other kids" is what she likes best about being a member. The response has been strong, with more than 36 juniors already enrolled at the Port St. Lucie location.

Diana Cowan Kempton, the club's program director, views chess as a tool for developing important life skills in young people. She believes the game can help build future leaders who are more focused, patient, strategic, and thoughtful when making decisions. The Atlantis Chess Club currently meets every Friday at its Port St. Lucie location. The program has generated enough interest and success that expansion plans are underway.

The club's growth reflects Baptiste's goal of introducing more young people to chess and changing community attitudes toward board games. With over 30 members already engaged and two additional programs planned for the Fenn Center in Fort Pierce, the initiative shows no signs of slowing down. What started as one boy's desire to share his love of chess has turned into a thriving community resource that offers both recreational play and skill development for children of all abilities.
